messages:
morgan: Heads-up — thinking about tenant migration/lease semantics for multi-region active/active. Specifically: how small can our heartbeat/grace window be before we break residency guarantees for EU tenants?

ria: tl;dr: smaller = faster failover but higher risk of split-brain & accidental cross-border writes. for residency we need explicit resident-region write-locks + read-routing policy.

diego: Agree. We currently treat residency as a soft-affinity + write-leases. If a non-resident region gets a request during a brief outage, we can serve reads but must not accept persistent writes unless the tenant opted into cross-region.

morgan: Right. Would like to propose a new default: 45s heartbeat + 90s grace before automatic migration. That keeps churn low but still recovers quick-ish. Thoughts?

ria: 45/90 seems reasonable for general customers. For regulated tenants we should allow org-level override to 5m/10m.

jamie: Also important: how do we surface this in Console and API? Need to show current lease owner, lease-expires-at, and whether migration is in-progress. Users should be able to lock their residency.

morgan: +1. UX note: show a "migration ETA" and a one-click cancel for org admins during the grace window.

platform-bot: Deploy queued: infra/lease-manager v2.3 -> staging (sha: ef12a3). Changes include configurable heartbeat/grace windows.

diego: One implementation risk — if we pick 45s heartbeat with aggressive retry, we might overwhelm control plane during global blips. Need exponential backoff on lease attempts and jitter.

ria: Exactly. Proposal: client jitter + randomized lease-refresh offset per-tenancy:
```
lease: {
  heartbeat: 45s,
  grace: 90s,
  refresh_jitter: 0..6s,
  backoff: { base: 500ms, factor: 2, max: 30s }
}
```

morgan: Good. What about KV cache eviction & prefix cache ownership when we migrate? We can't evict everything immediately or we'll spike cold token cost.

diego: Plan: two-phase handoff. Phase A: soft-redirect reads to resident region (TTL reduce), warm caches in new writer region for pinned prefixes. Phase B: after grace window, owner flips and we atomically swap lease token + evict old cache entries lazily (LRU with prefer-new).

jamie: Does that require cross-region cache streaming? That has cost implications. Maybe we only stream hot prefixes above threshold to new owner during warm-up.

ria: Yes — only hot streaming. Add metrics: hot-prefix count, bytes transferred, and warm-up latency. Also add a flag to disable streaming for sensitive tenants.

morgan: What about failure modes: if the old owner is flapping but still responding slowly, we could get conflicting writes during the handoff window. How do we prevent double-commits?

diego: Use monotonic per-tenant commit epochs + write sequence numbers. During handoff the new owner must abort any writes with seq <= last-seen. We already have this for rolling upgrades; extend to cross-region handoffs.

ria: Another constraint: audit logs must record the exact moment of cross-border write allowance. If a tenant has "residency: EU-only" then any allowed cross-region write needs explicit admin opt-in and extra logging.

morgan: Ops playbook idea: when failover triggers for a regulated tenant, send an automated ticket to compliance with migration details and retention policy.

platform-bot: Note: runbook update candidate created: docs/runbooks/geo-lease-handoff.md (PR #622).

jamie: Performance question — what's the user-visible latency impact during warm-up? We should measure p50/p95 for first 10s/60s after migration. If it's > 200ms p95, it's going to be noisy.

diego: Expected impact depends on model size & kv-hit-rate. For text-gen workloads with large KV caches we might see 40-80ms extra p95 if hot prefixes are migrated proactively. Cold cases will be worse.

ria: Action items: 1) Lock default policy to 45s/90s with org override; 2) Implement refresh_jitter + backoff; 3) Two-phase cache handoff with hot-prefix streaming; 4) Epoch-based commit sequencing extension; 5) Console flags and audit event.

morgan: I'll draft an RFC summary and add a tiny state-machine diagram. Anyone want to co-author?

jamie: I can add Console/UI bits.

diego: Happy to write the sequence-number tests and failure-mode sims.

ria: I'll handle the compliance/audit hook and org-overrides.

morgan: Great. leaving a note here for the follow-up meeting — schedule 30m sync Thursday to finalize defaults. :calendar: 

platform-bot: Reminder: scheduled sync created — #infra-arch sync Thu 10:00 UTC.

morgan: Thanks all. Closing thread unless someone has more objections.

ria: No objections from me.

diego: LGTM.

jamie: LGTM.
